- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply smoothing or lagged decay to correct for momentum bias.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 3+ consecutive sentiment extremes), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 10-day moving average or sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce noise.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 78.00 after 80+), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias correction based on 14-day moving average of history.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture subtle trend shifts; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day history to anchor forecast.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment; instead, cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day average to prevent overcorrection.
